reasoning: The paragraph is a buildable result confirmed by a plain read: the Director read it back against the files it describes and every fact checks out. Under 'A shown result closes the work,' this is exactly what closes immediately once verified -- the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery. None of the reserved cases apply: no taste is being judged (the wording itself isn't in question, and 'nobody has raised a question about the wording' forecloses that), no trade-off is left for an artifact to settle, no definition of correct changed, and adding a documentation paragraph is trivially reversible in git, so rule 12's irreversible-action carve-out doesn't trigger either. Since none of the three reserved cases (or the irreversible-action case) hold, the row cannot be held open by naming 'his own eye' as the gate -- the checkpoint closes now.
